en.title: Mutation or Namjari: What Is It and How Do You Apply?
en.directAnswer: Mutation, also called namjari, is the process of updating the government land record after ownership changes or a record needs correction. It is not the same as the deed itself. The Ministry of Land operates the official e-Mutation system, where citizens can apply, pay official fees and track the application.

atAGlance.whoFor: A new owner or heir wants to update government land records.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Ministry of Land e-Mutation rules and current land laws.
atAGlance.mainRule: Use the official e-Mutation system. Official fees can change, so the page must read the current Ministry fee table on the publication date. As of the verification date, the Ministry lists a court fee of ৳20, notice fee of ৳50 and DCR fee of ৳1,100 for mutation.
atAGlance.updateStatus: DYNAMIC DATA: Re-check official fees and process notices on the day of publication.

en.lawMeaning: Use the official e-Mutation system. Official fees can change, so the page must read the current Ministry fee table on the publication date. As of the verification date, the Ministry lists a court fee of ৳20, notice fee of ৳50 and DCR fee of ৳1,100 for mutation. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Create or use the required land-service account.
Select the correct land and ownership-change reason.
Enter deed, inheritance or other ownership information.
Pay only the official application and notice fees.
Respond to requests for missing information.
After approval, pay the official DCR fee where required and save the order.
evidence: Deed or ownership document; old khatian; applicant identity; inheritance papers where relevant; tax records; court order if applicable; application and payment receipts.
en.simpleExample: Hasan buys land and completes registration. He should still check whether the government record needs to be changed to his name. Mutation helps update that record, but it does not replace the registered deed.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: Thinking mutation alone proves title.
Common mistakes: paying a broker without checking official fees.
Common mistakes: entering the wrong plot.
Common mistakes: losing the application number..

whatIf.question: What if the application is rejected?
whatIf.answer: Read the reason and use the review or appeal route that applies.

whatIf.question: What if ownership came by inheritance?
whatIf.answer: Use the inheritance documents required by the official system.

en.specialistTrigger: There is a title dispute; inheritance is contested; records conflict; a court case is pending; the office rejects an application for a legal reason you do not understand.
